encounter_greeting.text: Well met, ser {player}. I am {persona} of {my_faction}, and it does my heart good to see a friendly banner on this road.
Hail, traveller. I am {persona}, sworn to {my_faction}. State your business plainly and we shall see what the road requires of us.
Halt, ser {player}. {persona} of {my_faction} stands in your path, and I will not yield the road without good reason.
Ser {player}, I am {persona} of {my_faction}. My oat-field waits for me at home, but I can spare a moment for an honest companion.

encounter_threatened.text: You would have {gold} gold from me, ser {player}? Tesnovar does not buy its way out of a road. Draw your steel or ride on.
Ser {player}, a demand for {gold} gold is a poor way to greet a man of the Wardenry. My purse is light, but my honour is not for sale.
Threats and {gold} gold in one breath, ser {player}? I have heard braver demands from better men, and they lie in the ground now.
Put up your demand, ser {player}. Asking {gold} gold of me changes nothing. I shall answer with my oath, not my coin.

encounter_alliance_yes.text: Ser {player}, I accept. Let our banners stand together against {enemy_faction}, and may the ancestors witness this bargain.
An alliance, ser {player}? Very well, I accept. Mind that you do not sell me to {rival} at the first lantern we pass.
I take your hand gladly, ser {player}. Against {enemy_faction} we shall stand, and I shall carry a debt to you that I will not forget.
Agreed, ser {player}. The Wardenry keeps its word and so shall I. Do not make me regret it before we have crossed the next ford.

encounter_alliance_no.text: No alliance, ser {player}. I have seen what your banners do when the wind turns. Ride on before I change my mind.
I must decline, ser {player}. Ally with {rival} if you must, but I shall keep my oath to my own banner.
Your offer is refused, ser {player}. The ancestors would weep to see the Wardenry bound to one who breaks faith so easily.
I would be glad of your friendship, ser {player}, but an alliance I cannot give today. Forgive me, and let us meet again on kinder roads.

captured_by_player.text: So, ser {player}, the road has taken me. Very well. The Wardenry will not forget that I was bested, and neither will I. Name your ransom, {gold} gold, I suppose.
I yield to you, ser {player}, for now. Take me to {my_faction} if you must, but know that this is a debt the ancestors will collect.
Captured at last. Ser {player}, I shall not beg. My freedom costs {gold} gold, and I will pay it from my own purse, not from my people's.
You fought fairly, ser {player}, and I bear you no shame for the victory. Hold me as you must, but {my_faction} will come for its own.

released_by_player.text: Ser {player}, you let me go when a ransom would have served you. My oath is yours now. The ancestors will hear of this mercy.
Ser {player} released me without ransom. The Wardenry honours mercy shown, and I shall repay it in kind on some future road.
Ser {player} let me go free rather than take my ransom. I owe a debt I did not expect to owe, and I will not forget it.
You loosed me, ser {player}, and I will not thank you for a kindness wrapped around an insult. Mark that I remember both.

player_left_my_faction.text: Ser {player} has left {my_faction} for {faction}. A broken oath is a stain on any banner. Let the ancestors judge.
You turned your back on {my_faction} for {faction}, ser {player}. I shall not pretend it did not happen, nor forgive it lightly.
Ser {player} has gone over to {faction} and left {my_faction} behind. Each man weighs his own oath, I suppose. I shall weigh this one.
Ser {player}, I hear you now carry the banner of {faction}. Whatever you decide, I hope the road you chose is an honest one.

war_declared.text: {my_faction} has declared war on {enemy_faction}. Let the banners rise, and may the ancestors guard those who march.
Word has come that {enemy_faction} stands against {my_faction}. I shall march when the Wardenry calls, and not one step before.
War with {enemy_faction}, then. The oath of the Wardenry is older than this quarrel, and it will outlast it too.
{enemy_faction} has made its choice, and so has {my_faction}. I pray the ancestors grant us steady hands in the coming war.

fought_alongside_player.text: Ser {player}, we held the line together and {troop_count} of the enemy fell before {enemy_faction} broke. I shall tell this tale to my children.
That was well fought, ser {player}. We carried the field with {troop_count} of our own standing still. I owe you a share of it.
Ser {player}, my thanks for the shield at my side. Together we drove back {enemy_faction}, and I shall not forget it.

encounter_farewell.text: Fare well, ser {player}. May your road be dry and your banners unbroken. We shall meet again, I trust.
Go with the light, ser {player}. I have said my piece, and my road lies on. Keep your distance from my oats.
Begone, ser {player}. Our business is finished for now, but I do not forget the look you gave me. Mind the road ahead.
Ride on, then. The Wardenry does not hold grudges lightly, ser {player}, and neither do the ancestors. Take care of yourself.

ambient_chatter.text: Rain has fallen on {village} all morning, and my oats are sulking for it. Patience is a farmer's first virtue, or so my father always said.
Bread from {town} is a poor thing beside the loaves of home. Still, hunger is no respecter of honour, so I shall eat it gladly.
They say the Chorvena ford ran high this week. I have sworn never to march beyond it, and I count that a blessing this season.
Weary legs and a full heart, that is the Wardenry's way. I shall sleep well in {village} tonight, with the ancestors watching over me.
